summary: Concentrated: 55 holdings, but the top ten are 77% of the portfolio.
Trades a lot: about 172% of the portfolio changes in a year.
The average holding, by value, has been owned for 0.5 years.
Compared with the typical S&P 500 company, its holdings are more expensive, faster-growing and much larger.
Copying each filing beat the S&P 500 in 4 of 6 full years.

profile.background: Chief investment officer of Viking Global before founding D1 Capital Partners in July 2018 with more than $500 million of his own money.
profile.approach: Long and short stock-picking with medium- to long-term horizons, plus late-stage private companies.
known: Returned 60% in 2020, then lost about $4 billion (20% of capital) in the January 2021 GameStop short squeeze; recovered most of it by April.
Private investments have included Robinhood and Instacart.
profile.note: The 13F shows long positions only, not short positions or private holdings.

name: Dan Sundheim
